items.title: Finiteness, birationality and the reduced case for the normalization of a locally algebraic scheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally algebraic scheme X over a field k with normalization nu, the four-part lemma collects the expected properties: finiteness and dominance with a disjoint union of normal irreducible pieces, the factorization through the reduced scheme with the first map the normalization of the reduced scheme, birationality in the reduced algebraic case, and the variety case (statement lines 4902-4918). Part (1) is assembled in the proof: local Noetherianness gives finitely many irreducible components on quasi-compact opens so the definition of the normalization applies, the normalization is always a disjoint union of normal integral schemes with dominant morphism, and finiteness comes from the fact that a locally finite type scheme over a field is universally Nagata (proof lines 4920-4936). Part (4) then has a short argument of its own: separatedness of the normalization because it is finite over a separated scheme, combined with the previous parts (proof lines 4945-4946). Parts (2) and (3) are stated by the author as direct references to the Morphisms chapter (proof lines 4938-4942). The claim is H2: the content is the assembly in part (1) and the one-line argument for (4), with the rest being standard normalization facts.
